Let \(b\) be the number of black balls and \(T=n+b\). The probability is
\[
\frac{n}{T}\cdot \frac{b}{T-1}=\frac{n}{100}.
\]
Canceling \(n>0\):
\[
\frac{b}{T(T-1)}=\frac1{100},
\]
so
\[
T(T-1)=100b.
\]
Thus \(100\mid T(T-1)\). Since \(T\) and \(T-1\) are consecutive, the divisibility by \(4\) and \(25\) must split between them.

Also \(b\ge2\) and \(n=T-b\ge2\), so \(15\le T\le 98\). The valid solutions are
\[
T=25 \quad \text{or} \quad T=76.
\]
For \(T=25\):
\[
b=\frac{25\cdot24}{100}=6,\qquad n=25-6=19.
\]
For \(T=76\):
\[
b=\frac{76\cdot75}{100}=57,\qquad n=76-57=19.
\]
Thus the answer is
\[
\boxed{19}
\]
